title: The colimit of an inverse system of sites with finite coverings
statement: Let $\mathcal I$ be a cofiltered category; for $i\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal I)$ let $\mathcal C_i$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] all of whose coverings have finite index sets; for $a:i\to j$ in $\mathcal I$ let $f_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ be a morphism of sites given by a continuous functor $u_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$, with $f_a\circ f_b=f_c$ (i.e. $u_b\circ u_a=u_c$) whenever $c=a\circ b$, and $u_{\mathrm{id}_i}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C_i}$ (so the $u_a$ form a functor $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Cat}$, the diagram whose colimit is used below; Stacks Sites, Situation 0A34 and the proof of Lemma 09YL). Let $\mathcal C=\varinjlim\mathcal C_i$ be the category with $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)=\varinjlim\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_i)$ and $\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C)=\varinjlim\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C_i)$ (filtered colimits of sets along the maps induced by the $u_a$), with source, target and composition inherited, and $u_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C$ the canonical functors; let $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ be the union of the images under the $u_i$ of the sets $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C_i)$. Then: (1) $(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C))$ is a site, and every finite diagram in $\mathcal C$ is the image under some $u_i$ of a diagram in $\mathcal C_i$ (Sites, Lemma 09YL). (2) Each $u_i$ is continuous and defines a morphism of sites $f_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_i$, with $f_a\circ f_j=f_i$ for $a:j\to i$ (as $u_a$ followed by $u_j$ is $u_i$); for $U_i\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_i)$ and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C_i$, $f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(u_i(U_i))=\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}f_a^{-1}\mathcal F(u_a(U_i))$ (Sites, Lemma 0A35); the same formula holds for an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C_i$, with $f_i^{-1}$, $f_a^{-1}$ the inverse images of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

proof.text: *The colimit category.* For $c=a\circ b$ in $\mathcal I$ ($a:j\to i$, $b:k\to j$) the morphism of sites $f_a\circ f_b$ is given by the functor $u_b\circ u_a$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], composition of morphisms of sites, Sites 03CB), so $f_a\circ f_b=f_c$ means $u_b\circ u_a=u_{a\circ b}$; also $u_{\mathrm{id}_i}=\mathrm{id}$. Since $\mathcal I$ is cofiltered, $\mathcal J=\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ is filtered, and $a^{\mathrm{op}}\mapsto u_a$ is a system of categories over $\mathcal J$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories] (the underlying categories of sites have sets of objects and morphisms, Sites 00VH). That node gives the category $\mathcal C=\varinjlim\mathcal C_i$ of the statement (objects and arrows the filtered colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), whose objects and morphisms form sets, the functors $u_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C$ with $u_j\circ u_a=u_i$ for $a:j\to i$, and: (A) every finite diagram of $\mathcal C$ (finitely many objects and morphisms with finitely many source/target/composition/identity relations) is the image under $u_i$ of a diagram in $\mathcal C_i$ satisfying the same relations, for some $i$, and two lifts agree after applying suitable $u_b$, $u_{b'}$ to a common later stage; (B) for $X,Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_i)$, $\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aX,u_aY)\cong\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(u_iX,u_iY)$ via $\beta\mapsto u_j(\beta)$, the colimit over the arrows $a:j\to i$ (filtered, being $(\mathcal I/i)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\mathcal I/i$ cofiltered by [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion](0)); (C) a morphism of $\mathcal C$ is an isomorphism iff it is $u_j$ of an isomorphism of some $\mathcal C_j$. In particular the second assertion of (1) of the statement (finite diagrams come from some $\mathcal C_i$) is (A). $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)=\bigcup_iu_i(\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C_i))$ is a set, a union over the set $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal I)$ of images of sets.

proof.text: *Moving data to a later stage.* Every continuous $u_a$ ($a:j\to i$) carries a covering $\{U^t_i\to U_i\}$ of $\mathcal C_i$ to a covering of $\mathcal C_j$ and carries the fibre products $U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i$ (which exist, Sites 00VH axiom (3)) to fibre products $u_a(U^t_i)\times_{u_a(U_i)}u_a(V_i)$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], Sites 00WV). Consequently: given a covering $\mathcal U=\{U^t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ of $\mathcal C$, so $\mathcal U=u_k(\mathcal U_k)$ for a covering $\mathcal U_k$ of some $\mathcal C_k$, and finitely many further objects and morphisms of $\mathcal C$ related to $\mathcal U$ by finitely many relations (for instance a morphism $V\to U$), there are, for every given $i$, an object $j$ with an arrow $a:j\to i$ and a covering $\mathcal U_j$ of $\mathcal C_j$ together with lifts of the further data to $\mathcal C_j$, satisfying the relations, whose image under $u_j$ is the given data: choose $j$ with arrows to $i$, to $k$ and to a stage where the further data lift (cofilteredness of $\mathcal I$), push $\mathcal U_k$ and the lifts to $\mathcal C_j$ by the corresponding $u$'s (a covering stays a covering), and pass to a later stage where the finitely many relations, which hold in $\mathcal C$, already hold (step 1 (A)); pushing along a further $u_b$ keeps all of this. The same applies to finitely many coverings simultaneously.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09YL, second paragraph ('By our remark above and our definition of coverings, we can find an i, a covering ... and a morphism V_i -> U_i whose image by u_i is the given data ... In particular we can replace i by j')

proof.text: *Fibre products in $\mathcal C$ (axiom (3)).* Let $\{U^t\to U\}$ be a covering of $\mathcal C$ and $V\to U$ a morphism. By step 2 they are $u_i$ of a covering $\{U^t_i\to U_i\}$ of $\mathcal C_i$ and a morphism $V_i\to U_i$. Claim: $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)$ with the $u_i$-images of the two projections is a fibre product $U^t\times_UV$ in $\mathcal C$. Let $W$ be an object of $\mathcal C$; by step 2 (replacing $i$ by some $j\to i$ and the data by their $u_a$-images, which by continuity are again a covering, a morphism and their fibre product) we may assume $W=u_i(W_i)$. By step 1 (B), $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i))=\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_a(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i))$; by continuity of $u_a$ the latter set is $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_aU^t_i)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_aU_i)}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_aV_i)$, compatibly with the transition maps; the filtered colimit over $a$ commutes with this fibre product of sets [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits], and applying step 1 (B) to the three factors gives $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,U^t)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,U)}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,V)$, the composite bijection being composition with the images of the projections. So $U^t\times_UV$ exists and equals $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)$, and $\{U^t\times_UV\to V\}=u_i(\{U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i\to V_i\})$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$, since $\{U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i\to V_i\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_i$ (axiom (3) for $\mathcal C_i$). This is axiom (3) of Sites, Definition 00VH. In addition: for every covering $\{U^t_i\to U_i\}$ of $\mathcal C_i$ and morphism $V_i\to U_i$, $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)\to u_i(U^t_i)\times_{u_i(U_i)}u_i(V_i)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: *Axiom (2).* Let $\{U^t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ be a covering of $\mathcal C$ and for each $t$ let $\{U^{ts}\to U^t\}_{s\in S_t}$ be a covering of $\mathcal C$. Since $T$ is finite (every covering of every $\mathcal C_i$ has a finite index set, hence so does every covering of $\mathcal C$), step 2 applied to the finitely many coverings and the relations 'the target of the $t$-th covering is the $t$-th member of the first' gives $j$, a covering $\{U^t_j\to U_j\}$ of $\mathcal C_j$ and coverings $\{U^{ts}_j\to U^t_j\}$ of $\mathcal C_j$ whose images under $u_j$ are the given ones. By axiom (2) for $\mathcal C_j$, $\{U^{ts}_j\to U_j\}_{t,s}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_j$, and its image $\{U^{ts}\to U\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. (Without finiteness of $T$ the $t$-th covering might only come from stages that have no common lower bound.)

proof.text: *Axiom (1), and conclusion of (1).* Let $\varphi:V\to U$ be an isomorphism of $\mathcal C$. By step 1 (C), $\varphi=u_j(\gamma)$ for an isomorphism $\gamma:V_j\to U_j$ of some $\mathcal C_j$; by axiom (1) for $\mathcal C_j$, $\{\gamma\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_j$, so $\{\varphi\}=u_j(\{\gamma\})$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. With steps 3 and 4, $(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C))$ satisfies the axioms of Sites, Definition 00VH (its objects and coverings form sets by step 1), i.e. it is a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; with step 1 (A) this proves (1) of the statement. (Stacks omits the proof of this axiom.)

proof.text: *Continuity of $u_i$ and compatibility.* $u_i$ carries coverings of $\mathcal C_i$ to coverings of $\mathcal C$ by the definition of $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$, and $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)\to u_i(U^t_i)\times_{u_i(U_i)}u_i(V_i)$ is an isomorphism by the last assertion of step 3; so $u_i$ is continuous (Sites 00WV, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]). Hence $u_i^s:\mathcal H\mapsto\mathcal H\circ u_i$ carries sheaves on $\mathcal C$ to sheaves on $\mathcal C_i$ and has the left adjoint $u_{i,s}$; it remains to show that $u_{i,s}$ is exact (steps 7-12), so that $u_i$ defines a morphism of sites $f_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_i$ with $f_i^{-1}=u_{i,s}$, $f_{i*}=u_i^s$. Once this is shown, $f_a\circ f_j$ is the morphism of sites given by $u_j\circ u_a=u_i$ (Sites 03CB, as in step 1), i.e. $f_a\circ f_j=f_i$ for $a:j\to i$.

proof.text: *Right exactness.* $u_{i,s}$ is left adjoint to $u_i^s$, so it commutes with all colimits that exist [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], in particular with finite colimits (Categories, Lemma 0039). So exactness of $u_{i,s}$ reduces to left exactness, i.e. commutation with finite limits (step 12).

proof.text: *Transition maps.* Fix $i$ and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C_i$. For $a:j\to i$ put $\mathcal P_a=u_{a,s}\mathcal F=f_a^{-1}\mathcal F$, a sheaf on $\mathcal C_j$, with unit $\eta_a:\mathcal F\to u_a^s\mathcal P_a$; since $u_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$, $\eta_{\mathrm{id}}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal P_{\mathrm{id}}$ is an isomorphism. For $b:k\to j$ we have $u_{a\circ b}^s=u_a^s\circ u_b^s$ (both are $\mathcal H\mapsto\mathcal H\circ u_b\circ u_a$, step 1); let $\tau_{a,b}:\mathcal P_a\to u_b^s\mathcal P_{a\circ b}$ be the map corresponding under $u_{a,s}\dashv u_a^s$ to $\eta_{a\circ b}:\mathcal F\to u_{a\circ b}^s\mathcal P_{a\circ b}=u_a^s(u_b^s\mathcal P_{a\circ b})$; concretely maps $\tau_{a,b}(W):\mathcal P_a(W)\to\mathcal P_{a\circ b}(u_bW)$, natural in $W\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$ and in $\mathcal F$. Then $\tau_{a,\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tau_{a,b\circ c}=u_b^s(\tau_{a\circ b,c})\circ\tau_{a,b}$ for $c:l\to k$: both sides correspond to $\eta_{a\circ b\circ c}$, because $u_a^s(u_b^s\tau_{ab,c}\circ\tau_{a,b})\circ\eta_a=u_{ab}^s(\tau_{ab,c})\circ\eta_{ab}=\eta_{abc}$ by the definition of $\tau_{a,b}$ and of $\tau_{ab,c}$. Moreover $\tau_{\mathrm{id},a}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}=\eta_a$ (by definition). (In Stacks these maps are implicit in 'f_a^{-1}' and the identification $f_b^{-1}f_a^{-1}=f_{a\circ b}^{-1}$; for $u$ continuous, $\tau_{a,b}$ is the adjunct of that canonical isomorphism, but only the adjunction is used here.)

proof.text: *The presheaf $\mathcal G$.* For $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ let $T_V$ be the category whose objects are triples $t=(j,a,W)$ with $a:j\to i$ in $\mathcal I$, $W\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$, $u_j(W)=V$, a morphism $(k,a',W')\to(j,a,W)$ being a $b:k\to j$ with $a\circ b=a'$ and $u_b(W)=W'$; and $M_V:T_V^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Sets}$, $(j,a,W)\mapsto\mathcal P_a(W)$, $b\mapsto\tau_{a,b}(W)$ (a functor by the cocycle identity of step 8). For $t=(j,a,W)$ let $\Psi_t:\mathcal I/j\to T_V$, $(b:k\to j)\mapsto(k,a\circ b,u_bW)$. $\Psi_t$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion](1) ($\mathcal I/j$ is cofiltered by its part (0)): (i) given $t'=(j',a',W')$, cofilteredness gives $b:k\to j$, $b':k\to j'$ with $a\circ b=a'\circ b'$ (first a common lower bound, then an equalizing arrow); as $u_k(u_bW)=V=u_k(u_{b'}W')$, by step 1 (A) there is $e:l\to k$ with $u_{be}W=u_{b'e}W'$, and then $b'\circ e$ is a morphism $\Psi_t(b\circ e)\to t'$; (ii) two morphisms $s,s':\Psi_t(b)\to t''$ are arrows $c,c':k\to j''$ with equal composites to $i$ and equal effect on objects; an arrow $d:l\to k$ with $c\circ d=c'\circ d$ (cofilteredness) is a morphism $b\circ d\to b$ of $\mathcal I/j$ with $s\circ\Psi_t(d)=s'\circ\Psi_t(d)$. $T_V$ is nonempty ($V=u_k(W_k)$ for some $k$; take $j$ with arrows $e:j\to k$, $a:j\to i$ and $(j,a,u_eW_k)$). Hence $\Psi_t$ is initial, $T_V$ is cofiltered, and $\mathcal G(V):=\varinjlim_{T_V^{\mathrm{op}}}M_V$ (filtered colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) satisfies $\mathcal G(V)=\varinjlim_{b:k\to j}\mathcal P_{a\circ b}(u_bW)$ via the coprojections $\iota_{(k,ab,u_bW)}$, for every $t=(j,a,W)\in T_V$. Every element of $\mathcal G(V)$ is $\iota_t(x)$ for some $t$ and $x$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. *Restriction maps.* For $\alpha:V'\to V$ in $\mathcal C$ choose (step 1 (A)) $j$, $a:j\to i$ and $\alpha_j:W'\to W$ in $\mathcal C_j$ with $u_j(\alpha_j)=\alpha$ (first lift $\alpha$ at some stage, then push to a stage over $i$), and let $\mathcal G(\alpha):\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V')$ be the colimit over $b:k\to j$ of the maps $\mathcal P_{ab}(u_b\alpha_j):\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bW)\to\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bW')$ (compatible with the transition maps by naturality of $\tau_{ab,c}$ in $W$), using the two presentations above. It is characterized by $\mathcal G(\alpha)\circ\iota_{(k,ab,u_bW)}=\iota_{(k,ab,u_bW')}\circ\mathcal P_{ab}(u_b\alpha_j)$, and the same identity then holds for every lift $\alpha'_{j'}:W'_1\to W_1$ of $\alpha$ at any stage over $i$: two lifts become equal after pushing to a common later stage (step 1 (A)), and the identity is stable under pushing (naturality of $\tau$); by the elementwise description this determines $\mathcal G(\alpha)$, so $\mathcal G(\alpha)$ does not depend on the choice. Lifting a composable pair $\alpha,\beta$ and $\beta\circ\alpha$ at one stage (step 1 (A)) and using functoriality of the $\mathcal P_a$ gives $\mathcal G(\beta\circ\alpha)=\mathcal G(\alpha)\circ\mathcal G(\beta)$ and $\mathcal G(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. So $\mathcal G$ is a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, functorial in $\mathcal F$ (the $\mathcal P_a$ and $\tau$ are).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A35, second paragraph (definition of $\mathcal G(V)=\colim_{b:k\to j}f_{a\circ b}^{-1}\mathcal F(u_b(V_j))$; independence of choices and presheaf property 'omitted' there, written out here by the agent)

proof.text: *$\mathcal G$ is a sheaf.* Let $\mathcal U=\{U^t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ be a covering of $\mathcal C$ ($T$ finite). By step 2 there are $a:j\to i$ and a covering $\mathcal U_j=\{U^t_j\to U_j\}$ of $\mathcal C_j$ with $u_j(\mathcal U_j)=\mathcal U$, and by step 3 $U^t\times_UU^{t'}=u_j(U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j)$. For $b:k\to j$, $u_b(\mathcal U_j)$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_k$ and $u_b(U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j)=u_bU^t_j\times_{u_bU_j}u_bU^{t'}_j$ (continuity), so, $\mathcal P_{a\circ b}$ being a sheaf, $\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bU_j)\to\prod_t\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bU^t_j)\rightrightarrows\prod_{t,t'}\mathcal P_{ab}(u_b(U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j))$ is an equalizer diagram; these diagrams are compatible with the maps $\tau$ as $b$ varies (naturality of $\tau$ in $W$). Pass to the filtered colimit over $b:k\to j$: by the presentations of step 9 at the objects $(j,a,U_j)$, $(j,a,U^t_j)$, $(j,a,U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j)$ and the characterization of the restriction maps, the colimit of the diagrams is $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod_t\mathcal G(U^t)\rightrightarrows\prod_{t,t'}\mathcal G(U^t\times_UU^{t'})$; filtered colimits of sets commute with finite products and equalizers [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] ($T$ finite), so it is again an equalizer. Hence $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf (Sites 00VM). (Stacks writes $f_{b\circ a}^{-1}$ in the displayed formula; the composite is $a\circ b$.)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A35, second paragraph ('In fact, G satisfies the sheaf condition ... The first equality holds because filtered colimits commute with finite limits (Categories, Lemma 002W)')

proof.text: *$\mathcal G=f_i^{-1}\mathcal F$, and the formula.* Let $\mathcal H$ be a sheaf on $\mathcal C$. (a) Given $\psi:\mathcal F\to u_i^s\mathcal H=u_a^s(u_j^s\mathcal H)$ ($u_j^s\mathcal H$ is a sheaf, $u_j$ being continuous, step 6), let $\psi_a:\mathcal P_a\to u_j^s\mathcal H$ be its adjunct under $u_{a,s}\dashv u_a^s$, i.e. maps $\psi_a(W):\mathcal P_a(W)\to\mathcal H(u_jW)$. Then $\psi_{a\circ b}(u_bW)\circ\tau_{a,b}(W)=\psi_a(W)$: both sides correspond to $\psi$, as $u_a^s(u_b^s\psi_{ab}\circ\tau_{a,b})\circ\eta_a=u_{ab}^s(\psi_{ab})\circ\eta_{ab}=\psi$ (step 8). So for every $V$ the maps $\psi_a(W)$, $(j,a,W)\in T_V$, form a cocone on $M_V$ and induce $\phi(V):\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal H(V)$, natural in $V$ by the characterization of $\mathcal G(\alpha)$ and the naturality of $\psi_a$. (b) Conversely, $\phi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ gives $\psi(U)=\phi(u_iU)\circ\iota_{(i,\mathrm{id},U)}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}(U):\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal H(u_iU)$, natural in $U$. (c) These are inverse bijections: starting from $\phi$, the maps $W\mapsto\phi(u_jW)\circ\iota_{(j,a,W)}$ form a morphism $\mathcal P_a\to u_j^s\mathcal H$ whose adjunct is $\psi$, since at $U\in\mathcal C_i$ it is $\phi(u_iU)\circ\iota_{(j,a,u_aU)}\circ\tau_{\mathrm{id},a}(U)\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}(U)=\phi(u_iU)\circ\iota_{(i,\mathrm{id},U)}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}(U)$ ($a$ is a morphism $(j,a,u_aU)\to(i,\mathrm{id},U)$ of $T_{u_iU}$, and $\tau_{\mathrm{id},a}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}=\eta_a$); so it equals $\psi_a$, and as every element of $\mathcal G(V)$ is some $\iota_{(j,a,W)}(x)$, $\phi$ is the map built from $\psi$ in (a); starting from $\psi$, (b) returns the adjunct of $\psi_{\mathrm{id}}$, which is $\psi$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C)}(\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)}(\mathcal F,u_i^s\mathcal H)$, naturally in $\mathcal H$ and in $\mathcal F$, so $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal G$ is a left adjoint of $u_i^s$ and is isomorphic to $u_{i,s}=f_i^{-1}$ by the unique isomorphism compatible with the units [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. Taking $t=(i,\mathrm{id},U_i)$ in step 9: $f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(u_i(U_i))=\mathcal G(u_i(U_i))=\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}\mathcal P_a(u_a(U_i))=\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}f_a^{-1}\mathcal F(u_a(U_i))$, the formula of (2); more generally $f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(u_j(W))=\varinjlim_{b:k\to j}f_{a\circ b}^{-1}\mathcal F(u_b(W))$ for $a:j\to i$ and $W\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$, naturally in $\mathcal F$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A35, third paragraph ('In this paragraph we check that G is canonically isomorphic to f_i^{-1}F ... This finishes the proof that G = f_i^{-1}F'), rewritten with the adjunct maps of step 8

proof.text: *Left exactness; $f_i$ is a morphism of sites; abelian sheaves.* Let $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and choose $(j,a,W)\in T_V$ (step 9). By step 11, $\mathcal F\mapsto f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(V)$ is, naturally in $\mathcal F$, the filtered colimit over $b:k\to j$ of the functors $\mathcal F\mapsto(u_{a\circ b,s}\mathcal F)(u_bW)$. Each of these commutes with finite limits: $u_{ab,s}=f_{ab}^{-1}$ is exact, $f_{ab}$ being a morphism of sites, and evaluation at an object commutes with finite limits of sheaves, which are computed sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise](1),(2); and filtered colimits of sets commute with finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits]. Hence $\mathcal F\mapsto f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(V)$ commutes with finite limits for every $V$, so $u_{i,s}$ does as a functor to presheaves [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise](1), hence as a functor to sheaves (a cone of sheaves that is a limit of presheaves is a limit of sheaves, sheaves forming a full subcategory). With step 7, $u_{i,s}$ is exact, so $u_i$ defines a morphism of sites $f_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_i$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], Sites 00X1), with $f_a\circ f_j=f_i$ by step 6. This proves (2) for sheaves of sets. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$, steps 8-11 go through verbatim in the categories of abelian sheaves ($u_{a,s}$, $u_{i,s}$ on abelian sheaves are the left adjoints of $u_a^s$, $u_i^s$ there [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the colimits $\mathcal G(V)$ are filtered colimits of abelian groups, whose underlying sets and finite limits are those of sets [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits], so the sheaf condition of step 10 holds; the adjunction argument of step 11 is the same with additive maps), which gives the formula for abelian sheaves.

old_proof.text: *The colimit category.* For $c=a\circ b$ in $\mathcal I$ ($a:j\to i$, $b:k\to j$) the morphism of sites $f_a\circ f_b$ is given by the functor $u_b\circ u_a$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], composition of morphisms of sites, Sites 03CB), so $f_a\circ f_b=f_c$ means $u_b\circ u_a=u_{a\circ b}$; also $u_{\mathrm{id}_i}=\mathrm{id}$. Since $\mathcal I$ is cofiltered, $\mathcal J=\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ is filtered, and $a^{\mathrm{op}}\mapsto u_a$ is a system of categories over $\mathcal J$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories] (the underlying categories of sites have sets of objects and morphisms, Sites 00VH). That node gives the category $\mathcal C=\varinjlim\mathcal C_i$ of the statement (objects and arrows the filtered colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), whose objects and morphisms form sets, the functors $u_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C$ with $u_j\circ u_a=u_i$ for $a:j\to i$, and: (A) every finite diagram of $\mathcal C$ (finitely many objects and morphisms with finitely many source/target/composition/identity relations) is the image under $u_i$ of a diagram in $\mathcal C_i$ satisfying the same relations, for some $i$, and two lifts agree after applying suitable $u_b$, $u_{b'}$ to a common later stage; (B) for $X,Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_i)$, $\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aX,u_aY)\cong\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(u_iX,u_iY)$ via $\beta\mapsto u_j(\beta)$, the colimit over the arrows $a:j\to i$ (filtered, being $(\mathcal I/i)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\mathcal I/i$ cofiltered by [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion](0)); (C) a morphism of $\mathcal C$ is an isomorphism iff it is $u_j$ of an isomorphism of some $\mathcal C_j$. In particular the second assertion of (1) of the statement (finite diagrams come from some $\mathcal C_i$) is (A). $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)=\bigcup_iu_i(\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C_i))$ is a set, a union over the set $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal I)$ of images of sets.

Claim: $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)$ with the $u_i$-images of the two projections is a fibre product $U^t\times_UV$ in $\mathcal C$. Let $W$ be an object of $\mathcal C$; by step 2 (replacing $i$ by some $j\to i$ and the data by their $u_a$-images, which by continuity are again a covering, a morphism and their fibre product) we may assume $W=u_i(W_i)$. By step 1 (B), $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i))=\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_a(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i))$; by continuity of $u_a$ the latter set is $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_aU^t_i)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_aU_i)}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_j}(u_aW_i,u_aV_i)$, compatibly with the transition maps; the filtered colimit over $a$ commutes with this fibre product of sets [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits], and applying step 1 (B) to the three factors gives $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,U^t)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,U)}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(W,V)$, the composite bijection being composition with the images of the projections. So $U^t\times_UV$ exists and equals $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)$, and $\{U^t\times_UV\to V\}=u_i(\{U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i\to V_i\})$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$, since $\{U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i\to V_i\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_i$ (axiom (3) for $\mathcal C_i$). This is axiom (3) of Sites, Definition 00VH. In addition: for every covering $\{U^t_i\to U_i\}$ of $\mathcal C_i$ and morphism $V_i\to U_i$, $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)\to u_i(U^t_i)\times_{u_i(U_i)}u_i(V_i)$ is an isomorphism.

Since $T$ is finite (every covering of every $\mathcal C_i$ has a finite index set, hence so does every covering of $\mathcal C$), step 2 applied to the finitely many coverings and the relations 'the target of the $t$-th covering is the $t$-th member of the first' gives $j$, a covering $\{U^t_j\to U_j\}$ of $\mathcal C_j$ and coverings $\{U^{ts}_j\to U^t_j\}$ of $\mathcal C_j$ whose images under $u_j$ are the given ones. By axiom (2) for $\mathcal C_j$, $\{U^{ts}_j\to U_j\}_{t,s}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_j$, and its image $\{U^{ts}\to U\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. old_proof.text: *Continuity of $u_i$ and compatibility.* $u_i$ carries coverings of $\mathcal C_i$ to coverings of $\mathcal C$ by the definition of $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$, and $u_i(U^t_i\times_{U_i}V_i)\to u_i(U^t_i)\times_{u_i(U_i)}u_i(V_i)$ is an isomorphism by the last assertion of step 3; so $u_i$ is continuous (Sites 00WV, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]). Hence $u_i^s:\mathcal H\mapsto\mathcal H\circ u_i$ carries sheaves on $\mathcal C$ to sheaves on $\mathcal C_i$ and has the left adjoint $u_{i,s}$; it remains to show that $u_{i,s}$ is exact (steps 7-12), so that $u_i$ defines a morphism of sites $f_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_i$ with $f_i^{-1}=u_{i,s}$, $f_{i*}=u_i^s$. Once this is shown, $f_j\circ f_a$ is the morphism of sites given by $u_j\circ u_a=u_i$ (Sites 03CB, as in step 1), i.e. $f_j\circ f_a=f_i$ for $a:j\to i$.

old_proof.text: *Transition maps.* Fix $i$ and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C_i$. For $a:j\to i$ put $\mathcal P_a=u_{a,s}\mathcal F=f_a^{-1}\mathcal F$, a sheaf on $\mathcal C_j$, with unit $\eta_a:\mathcal F\to u_a^s\mathcal P_a$; since $u_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$, $\eta_{\mathrm{id}}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal P_{\mathrm{id}}$ is an isomorphism. For $b:k\to j$ we have $u_{a\circ b}^s=u_a^s\circ u_b^s$ (both are $\mathcal H\mapsto\mathcal H\circ u_b\circ u_a$, step 1); let $\tau_{a,b}:\mathcal P_a\to u_b^s\mathcal P_{a\circ b}$ be the map corresponding under $u_{a,s}\dashv u_a^s$ to $\eta_{a\circ b}:\mathcal F\to u_{a\circ b}^s\mathcal P_{a\circ b}=u_a^s(u_b^s\mathcal P_{a\circ b})$; concretely maps $\tau_{a,b}(W):\mathcal P_a(W)\to\mathcal P_{a\circ b}(u_bW)$, natural in $W\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$ and in $\mathcal F$. Then $\tau_{a,\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tau_{a,b\circ c}=u_b^s(\tau_{a\circ b,c})\circ\tau_{a,b}$ for $c:l\to k$: both sides correspond to $\eta_{a\circ b\circ c}$, because $u_a^s(u_b^s\tau_{ab,c}\circ\tau_{a,b})\circ\eta_a=u_{ab}^s(\tau_{ab,c})\circ\eta_{ab}=\eta_{abc}$ by the definition of $\tau_{a,b}$ and of $\tau_{ab,c}$. Moreover $\tau_{\mathrm{id},a}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}=\eta_a$ (by definition). (In Stacks these maps are implicit in 'f_a^{-1}' and the identification $f_b^{-1}f_a^{-1}=f_{a\circ b}^{-1}$; for $u$ continuous, $\tau_{a,b}$ is the adjunct of that canonical isomorphism, but only the adjunction is used here.)

old_proof.text: *The presheaf $\mathcal G$.* For $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ let $T_V$ be the category whose objects are triples $t=(j,a,W)$ with $a:j\to i$ in $\mathcal I$, $W\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$, $u_j(W)=V$, a morphism $(k,a',W')\to(j,a,W)$ being a $b:k\to j$ with $a\circ b=a'$ and $u_b(W)=W'$; and $M_V:T_V^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Sets}$, $(j,a,W)\mapsto\mathcal P_a(W)$, $b\mapsto\tau_{a,b}(W)$ (a functor by the cocycle identity of step 8). For $t=(j,a,W)$ let $\Psi_t:\mathcal I/j\to T_V$, $(b:k\to j)\mapsto(k,a\circ b,u_bW)$. $\Psi_t$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion](1) ($\mathcal I/j$ is cofiltered by its part (0)): (i) given $t'=(j',a',W')$, cofilteredness gives $b:k\to j$, $b':k\to j'$ with $a\circ b=a'\circ b'$ (first a common lower bound, then an equalizing arrow); as $u_k(u_bW)=V=u_k(u_{b'}W')$, by step 1 (A) there is $e:l\to k$ with $u_{be}W=u_{b'e}W'$, and then $b'\circ e$ is a morphism $\Psi_t(b\circ e)\to t'$; (ii) two morphisms $s,s':\Psi_t(b)\to t''$ are arrows $c,c':k\to j''$ with equal composites to $i$ and equal effect on objects; an arrow $d:l\to k$ with $c\circ d=c'\circ d$ (cofilteredness) is a morphism $b\circ d\to b$ of $\mathcal I/j$ with $s\circ\Psi_t(d)=s'\circ\Psi_t(d)$. $T_V$ is nonempty ($V=u_k(W_k)$ for some $k$; take $j$ with arrows $e:j\to k$, $a:j\to i$ and $(j,a,u_eW_k)$). Hence $\Psi_t$ is initial, $T_V$ is cofiltered, and $\mathcal G(V):=\varinjlim_{T_V^{\mathrm{op}}}M_V$ (filtered colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) satisfies $\mathcal G(V)=\varinjlim_{b:k\to j}\mathcal P_{a\circ b}(u_bW)$ via the coprojections $\iota_{(k,ab,u_bW)}$, for every $t=(j,a,W)\in T_V$. Every element of $\mathcal G(V)$ is $\iota_t(x)$ for some $t$ and $x$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. *Restriction maps.* For $\alpha:V'\to V$ in $\mathcal C$ choose (step 1 (A)) $j$, $a:j\to i$ and $\alpha_j:W'\to W$ in $\mathcal C_j$ with $u_j(\alpha_j)=\alpha$ (first lift $\alpha$ at some stage, then push to a stage over $i$), and let $\mathcal G(\alpha):\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V')$ be the colimit over $b:k\to j$ of the maps $\mathcal P_{ab}(u_b\alpha_j):\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bW)\to\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bW')$ (compatible with the transition maps by naturality of $\tau_{ab,c}$ in $W$), using the two presentations above. It is characterized by $\mathcal G(\alpha)\circ\iota_{(k,ab,u_bW)}=\iota_{(k,ab,u_bW')}\circ\mathcal P_{ab}(u_b\alpha_j)$, and the same identity then holds for every lift $\alpha'_{j'}:W'_1\to W_1$ of $\alpha$ at any stage over $i$: two lifts become equal after pushing to a common later stage (step 1 (A)), and the identity is stable under pushing (naturality of $\tau$); by the elementwise description this determines $\mathcal G(\alpha)$, so $\mathcal G(\alpha)$ does not depend on the choice. Lifting a composable pair $\alpha,\beta$ and $\beta\circ\alpha$ at one stage (step 1 (A)) and using functoriality of the $\mathcal P_a$ gives $\mathcal G(\beta\circ\alpha)=\mathcal G(\alpha)\circ\mathcal G(\beta)$ and $\mathcal G(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. So $\mathcal G$ is a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, functorial in $\mathcal F$ (the $\mathcal P_a$ and $\tau$ are).

old_proof.text: *$\mathcal G$ is a sheaf.* Let $\mathcal U=\{U^t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ be a covering of $\mathcal C$ ($T$ finite). By step 2 there are $a:j\to i$ and a covering $\mathcal U_j=\{U^t_j\to U_j\}$ of $\mathcal C_j$ with $u_j(\mathcal U_j)=\mathcal U$, and by step 3 $U^t\times_UU^{t'}=u_j(U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j)$. For $b:k\to j$, $u_b(\mathcal U_j)$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_k$ and $u_b(U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j)=u_bU^t_j\times_{u_bU_j}u_bU^{t'}_j$ (continuity), so, $\mathcal P_{a\circ b}$ being a sheaf, $\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bU_j)\to\prod_t\mathcal P_{ab}(u_bU^t_j)\rightrightarrows\prod_{t,t'}\mathcal P_{ab}(u_b(U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j))$ is an equalizer diagram; these diagrams are compatible with the maps $\tau$ as $b$ varies (naturality of $\tau$ in $W$). Pass to the filtered colimit over $b:k\to j$: by the presentations of step 9 at the objects $(j,a,U_j)$, $(j,a,U^t_j)$, $(j,a,U^t_j\times_{U_j}U^{t'}_j)$ and the characterization of the restriction maps, the colimit of the diagrams is $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod_t\mathcal G(U^t)\rightrightarrows\prod_{t,t'}\mathcal G(U^t\times_UU^{t'})$; filtered colimits of sets commute with finite products and equalizers [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] ($T$ finite), so it is again an equalizer. Hence $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf (Sites 00VM). (Stacks writes $f_{b\circ a}^{-1}$ in the displayed formula; the composite is $a\circ b$.)

old_proof.text: *$\mathcal G=f_i^{-1}\mathcal F$, and the formula.* Let $\mathcal H$ be a sheaf on $\mathcal C$. (a) Given $\psi:\mathcal F\to u_i^s\mathcal H=u_a^s(u_j^s\mathcal H)$ ($u_j^s\mathcal H$ is a sheaf, $u_j$ being continuous, step 6), let $\psi_a:\mathcal P_a\to u_j^s\mathcal H$ be its adjunct under $u_{a,s}\dashv u_a^s$, i.e. maps $\psi_a(W):\mathcal P_a(W)\to\mathcal H(u_jW)$. Then $\psi_{a\circ b}(u_bW)\circ\tau_{a,b}(W)=\psi_a(W)$: both sides correspond to $\psi$, as $u_a^s(u_b^s\psi_{ab}\circ\tau_{a,b})\circ\eta_a=u_{ab}^s(\psi_{ab})\circ\eta_{ab}=\psi$ (step 8). So for every $V$ the maps $\psi_a(W)$, $(j,a,W)\in T_V$, form a cocone on $M_V$ and induce $\phi(V):\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal H(V)$, natural in $V$ by the characterization of $\mathcal G(\alpha)$ and the naturality of $\psi_a$. (b) Conversely, $\phi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ gives $\psi(U)=\phi(u_iU)\circ\iota_{(i,\mathrm{id},U)}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}(U):\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal H(u_iU)$, natural in $U$. (c) These are inverse bijections: starting from $\phi$, the maps $W\mapsto\phi(u_jW)\circ\iota_{(j,a,W)}$ form a morphism $\mathcal P_a\to u_j^s\mathcal H$ whose adjunct is $\psi$, since at $U\in\mathcal C_i$ it is $\phi(u_iU)\circ\iota_{(j,a,u_aU)}\circ\tau_{\mathrm{id},a}(U)\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}(U)=\phi(u_iU)\circ\iota_{(i,\mathrm{id},U)}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}(U)$ ($a$ is a morphism $(j,a,u_aU)\to(i,\mathrm{id},U)$ of $T_{u_iU}$, and $\tau_{\mathrm{id},a}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}}=\eta_a$); so it equals $\psi_a$, and as every element of $\mathcal G(V)$ is some $\iota_{(j,a,W)}(x)$, $\phi$ is the map built from $\psi$ in (a); starting from $\psi$, (b) returns the adjunct of $\psi_{\mathrm{id}}$, which is $\psi$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C)}(\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)}(\mathcal F,u_i^s\mathcal H)$, naturally in $\mathcal H$ and in $\mathcal F$, so $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal G$ is a left adjoint of $u_i^s$ and is isomorphic to $u_{i,s}=f_i^{-1}$ by the unique isomorphism compatible with the units [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. Taking $t=(i,\mathrm{id},U_i)$ in step 9: $f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(u_i(U_i))=\mathcal G(u_i(U_i))=\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}\mathcal P_a(u_a(U_i))=\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}f_a^{-1}\mathcal F(u_a(U_i))$, the formula of (2); more generally $f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(u_j(W))=\varinjlim_{b:k\to j}f_{a\circ b}^{-1}\mathcal F(u_b(W))$ for $a:j\to i$ and $W\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$, naturally in $\mathcal F$.

old_proof.text: *Left exactness; $f_i$ is a morphism of sites; abelian sheaves.* Let $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and choose $(j,a,W)\in T_V$ (step 9). By step 11, $\mathcal F\mapsto f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(V)$ is, naturally in $\mathcal F$, the filtered colimit over $b:k\to j$ of the functors $\mathcal F\mapsto(u_{a\circ b,s}\mathcal F)(u_bW)$. Each of these commutes with finite limits: $u_{ab,s}=f_{ab}^{-1}$ is exact, $f_{ab}$ being a morphism of sites, and evaluation at an object commutes with finite limits of sheaves, which are computed sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise](1),(2); and filtered colimits of sets commute with finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits]. Hence $\mathcal F\mapsto f_i^{-1}\mathcal F(V)$ commutes with finite limits for every $V$, so $u_{i,s}$ does as a functor to presheaves [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise](1), hence as a functor to sheaves (a cone of sheaves that is a limit of presheaves is a limit of sheaves, sheaves forming a full subcategory). With step 7, $u_{i,s}$ is exact, so $u_i$ defines a morphism of sites $f_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_i$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], Sites 00X1), with $f_j\circ f_a=f_i$ by step 6. This proves (2) for sheaves of sets. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$, steps 8-11 go through verbatim in the categories of abelian sheaves ($u_{a,s}$, $u_{i,s}$ on abelian sheaves are the left adjoints of $u_a^s$, $u_i^s$ there [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the colimits $\mathcal G(V)$ are filtered colimits of abelian groups, whose underlying sets and finite limits are those of sets [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits], so the sheaf condition of step 10 holds; the adjunction argument of step 11 is the same with additive maps), which gives the formula for abelian sheaves.
